description: An arpeggiator that can give each held note its own tempo, taken from the harmonic ratio of the interval it makes

params.text: Sets the tempo, doubling for every step of the knob about 120 bpm at its default, and spanning 15 bpm to 3840 bpm
Adds octaves to the pattern, one to five, the count shown by the colour of its lamp
Sets the order of the notes while POLYRHYTHM is off: ascending, descending, each note twice ascending, the order they were played, or random
Turns the polyrhythmic arpeggiator on and off; with it off the notes are arpeggiated one at a time
Holds the current pattern; releasing every note and playing a new one replaces it
Sets how much of each step the gate stays high, 0 to 100%

inputs.text: An external clock, read either as a voltage setting the tempo or as pulses per quarter note, according to the External Clock Mode on the menu
The notes to arpeggiate, one polyphonic channel per note
A gate holds its note in the pattern for as long as it is high

outputs.text: Carries the pitch of the note sounding, one polyphonic channel per held note while POLYRHYTHM is on
Carries a 5V gate for each note as the arpeggiator reaches it

notes: in the pulses-per-quarter-note clock modes the clock starts by itself when pulses arrive and stops when they stop
nothing is arpeggiated until notes arrive at the pitch input with gates at the gate input holding them in the pattern.
menu: External Clock Mode — how the EXT jack is read: CV (0V = 120 bpm), or 2 PPQN, 4 PPQN, 8 PPQN, 12 PPQN or 24 PPQN pulses per quarter note
Polyrhythm Mode — fixed fixes the ratios about C4 at 0V, which takes the tempo of the BPM knob; movable gives that tempo to the first note played and takes every other note's ratio from it
